Laura —

We cut over the private edge connection to Redwood this morning at 07:40 PST. Users behind our on-prem firewall are intermittently seeing traceroutes that stop after the first two hops, and application connections (HTTPS) to the service VIP sometimes hang and time out.

Symptoms:

- When we capture packets at our edge, we see SYNs reaching your edge, SYN-ACKs returning but some are dropped on the return path.
- Not consistent per-flow — appears to affect larger MTU flows and some client IP ranges.

We paused the cutover and rolled traffic back at 08:00 while we collect traces. Attaching a brief traceroute log.

Can you escalate networking? This is blocking our cutover.

Thanks for the pcap and traceroute — I took a quick pass. High-level observations:

- The pcap shows SYNs from client -> our edge VIP (no fragmentation on the outgoing segment). SYN-ACKs from our edge have the DF bit set and are larger (due to TCP options); we see ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages coming back to the edge for some replies but they are source-addressed to the SNAT pool IPs, not the original client IP.
- There are signs of asymmetric return path: some SYN-ACKs get routed through a transit hop that applies a SNAT, which then causes the ICMP message to go back to the SNAT IP and the edge drops it because the flow state doesn't match.

This looks like a combination of: MTU/PMTU sensitivity on larger TCP options AND SNAT asymmetry breaking ICMP-based PMTU discovery.

Immediate debug steps I recommend now:
1) Temporarily add an exception on FW1 for the client ranges so return traffic keeps original source IP (no SNAT) towards Redwood edge for testing.
2) If you can't remove SNAT, configure the SNAT device to forward ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages back to the original internal host or ensure it does not drop them.
3) Apply an MSS clamp on FW1 for TCP flows destined to the Redwood VIPs (1350) — should be quick and reversible.

If you can make step 1 or 3 changes, push them and let us know; we'll monitor for successful 3-way handshakes.

I can also test with a reduced MTU on our edge path temporarily if needed.

—Marissa Cole

Folks —

Adding a bit more detail from the edge side. Marissa's read matches our view. A couple technical notes and a recommended permanent fix:

- Root cause path: when the SYN-ACK is generated by our edge it may receive an ICMP PMTU reply via a different on-net transit path (NAT device). If that NAT rewrites the source, the ICMP doesn't map back to the TCP sockets and PMTU discovery fails. The socket then retransmits with DF set and the packets are dropped further upstream.

- Short-term: MSS clamp or lowering MTU on the VPN endpoint is the fastest, lowest-risk rollback.

- Medium/long-term: ensure that for traffic destined to Redwood VIPs your FW/transit devices preserve original source addresses (no SNAT) or at least properly translate ICMP back to the original host. Alternatively, establish a static route on the transit box so return flows don't traverse the SNAT path (i.e., avoid asymmetric egress).

Commands I would suggest your team run for confirmation:
- tcpdump -n -i <egress-if> host <client-ip> and port 443 to observe source IPs seen by firewall on return path
- ip route get <edge-vip> from <client-ip> to validate return nexthop

If you want, we can coordinate a short maintenance window to switch routing for the customer ranges to a no-SNAT egress. We'll standby if you schedule it.

—Jonas Weber
Network Lead, Private Deployments
